import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_16/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_16/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_16/training_2.csv"

# Source3_16_0: user info (user_id, gender, age, occupation, zip)
df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)

# Source3_16_1: ratings (user_id, movie_id, rating, timestamp)
df_source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Source3_16_2: movies (movie_id, title, genres)
df_source2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)

# Operation History Step 1: JOIN Source3_16_1 and Source3_16_2 on movie_id
# Join ratings with movie titles
df_joined = pd.merge(df_source1, df_source2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Operation History Step 2: group_by = [Source3_16_2.title]
# aggregations = [
#   avg(Source3_16_1.rating) filtered by gender='F' as F,
#   avg(Source3_16_1.rating) filtered by gender='M' as M
# ]

# To apply gender filter, we need gender info from Source3_16_0
# Join df_joined with df_source0 on user_id to get gender
df_joined = pd.merge(df_joined, df_source0[['gender']], left_on='user_id', right_index=True, how='left')

# Now group by title and calculate avg rating filtered by gender
# We will create two separate series for F and M, then join them

# Average rating for females per title
df_f = df_joined[df_joined['gender'] == 'F'].groupby('title')['rating'].mean().rename('F')

# Average rating for males per title
df_m = df_joined[df_joined['gender'] == 'M'].groupby('title')['rating'].mean().rename('M')

# Combine the two series into one DataFrame
df_result = pd.concat([df_f, df_m], axis=1).reset_index()

# Ensure columns are in the order: title, F, M
df_result = df_result[['title', 'F', 'M']]

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_16/target_multisource.csv"
df_result.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source files with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_16/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_16/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_16/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_16_1 and Source3_16_0 on user_id to get gender info for each rating
joined_1_0 = pd.merge(source1, source0[['user_id', 'gender']], on='user_id', how='inner')

# Join the above result with Source3_16_2 on movie_id to get movie titles
joined_all = pd.merge(joined_1_0, source2[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='inner')

# Filter ratings by gender and compute average rating per title for each gender
# Group by title only (string, leftmost column in target)
def avg_rating_by_gender(df, gender):
    return df.loc[df['gender'] == gender].groupby('title')['rating'].mean()

avg_f = avg_rating_by_gender(joined_all, 'F')
avg_m = avg_rating_by_gender(joined_all, 'M')

# Combine the two averages into one DataFrame
result = pd.DataFrame({
    'title': avg_f.index.union(avg_m.index)
}).set_index('title')

result['F'] = avg_f
result['M'] = avg_m

# Reset index to have title as a column
result = result.reset_index()

# Write to target file with exact column names
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_16/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
